Title: Navigation & Travel Drives
Description: Learn local navigation, in-system travel, and jump-gate routing between solar systems.

Steps.Title: Navigation Scale
Steps.Message: Subspace uses continuous travel at multiple scales. Fly normally for local maneuvering, use the in-system travel drive for long distances inside a solar system, and use physical jump gates for interstellar routes.

Steps.Title: System and Galaxy Maps
Steps.Message: Press M to open navigation. Use the system view for planets, moons, stations, belts, settlements and travel-drive destinations. Use the galaxy/sector view to inspect connected solar systems, security, known routes and jump-gate links.

Steps.Title: In-System Travel Drive
Steps.Message: Long trips inside one solar system are physical travel, not instant teleportation. Align to a valid destination, spool the drive, accelerate into cruise, then decelerate back into local flight. Gravity wells, hazards, interdiction and ship capability can affect the trip.

Steps.Title: Jump Gates
Steps.Message: Interstellar travel uses jump gates. Approach the gate, select a connected destination, satisfy access and ship restrictions, enter the capture corridor and transit through the warp tunnel. The same persistent ship exits the destination gate after the destination system is ready.

Steps.Title: Travel Planning
Steps.Message: Distance matters. Full-system travel is intentionally measured in minutes, remote settlements and resources can create logistics opportunities, and gate geography can make trade, security, exploration and fleet positioning strategically important.

Steps.Title: Open Navigation
Steps.Message: Press M to inspect your current system and known routes.

Steps.Title: Navigation Complete
Steps.Message: Use normal flight, the in-system travel drive and jump gates as one continuous travel hierarchy. Your ship, cargo, damage and crew remain persistent throughout the journey.
